contradiction_text: The cited research says agent-generated code adds more redundancy and technical debt per change even as reviewers feel better about approving it.
related_claim_texts: Agent-generated code can impose higher maintenance cost per change than human-written code, even when reviewers are more comfortable approving it.
The same cited research is described as finding that reviewers feel better about approving agent-generated code.
disclosure: Approval comfort should not be presented as evidence of code quality, because the provided material explicitly says higher reviewer confidence coexists with more redundancy and technical debt.

contradiction_text: The article treats passing tests and successful compilation as compatible with substantive defects, so green CI conflicts with any assumption that a clean run is sufficient evidence of correctness.
related_claim_texts: The article presents agent pull requests as a bounded correctness risk because code may pass compilation and tests while still containing substantive logic or security defects.
The article says the more dangerous hallucination is code that compiles, passes tests, and is still wrong.
disclosure: The draft should keep visible that test success is necessary but not sufficient, and that the source answers this tension only partially by requiring a failing pre-change test for non-trivial fixes.
